payload.query: Need complete brain MRI with contrast report (T1/T2/FLAIR/DWI, enhancement, perilesional edema, mass effect, serial size) and ventricular size or CSF flow study (core items to verify secondary headache from lesion versus obstructive hydrocephalus). Critical because 10 to 18 mm growth and mural nodule suggest neoplastic cystic lesion; ventricular assessment determines hydrocephalus contribution.
payload.retrieval_output: MRI showed a 10 mm cystic lesion with a mural nodule near the anterior horn of the right lateral ventricle. After a follow-up period of 10 years, the lesion started to increase in size from 10 to 18 mm, accompanied by worsening of headaches. MRI revealed that the increased size of the lesion was attributable to an enlargement of the cystic component and the mural nodule. A cystic mass with a gadolinium (Gd)-enhancing cyst wall and mural nodule were present. Signal intensity of the cystic component was high on T2-weighted imaging and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) imaging. The cyst wall and nodule showed low signal intensity on T2*-weighted imaging..
